T:treated-wastewater-outfall.title: Treated wastewater

U:alkylation.statement: This unit joins small gas molecules into larger ones, combining isobutane with olefins (reactive gases such as butylene) with a strong acid as the catalyst. The product, called alkylate, is a clean, high-octane petrol component.
U:alkylation.title: Alkylation (with acid regeneration)

U:amine.statement: This unit washes sour gas with a liquid called amine, which soaks up hydrogen sulphide. The amine is then heated to release the hydrogen sulphide and is reused, and the cleaned gas can be burned as fuel.
U:amine.title: Amine treating and regeneration

U:base-oil.statement: This plant makes lubricant base oil, the clean oil that lubricants and engine oils are blended from. It takes the oil left over from the hydrocracker, removes the waxy molecules and finishes it with hydrogen.
U:base-oil.title: Lubricant oil plant

U:buildings.statement: These are the non-process buildings on the site. They include the control room, offices, workshops, the laboratory, the warehouse, the fire station and the gatehouses.
U:buildings.title: Buildings (control rooms, admin, workshops, lab; layout only)

U:butamer.statement: This small unit converts normal butane, a gas with a straight chain of carbon atoms, into isobutane, the branched version. The two have the same atoms but behave differently in later reactions.
U:butamer.title: Butamer (butane isomerisation)

U:ccr-reformer.statement: The reformer rearranges the molecules in heavy naphtha to raise the octane rating, which is the measure of how well a fuel resists knocking in an engine. The catalyst is moved out continuously, cleaned and put back, which is what the letters CCR stand for, and hydrogen comes off as a useful by-product.
U:ccr-reformer.title: CCR reformer

U:cdu.statement: This is the first big step in any refinery. It heats crude oil until it boils and splits it into rough fractions: gases, naphtha (the raw material for petrol), kerosene (jet fuel), diesel and a heavy leftover called residue.
U:cdu.title: Crude distillation unit (desalters, preflash, atmospheric column)

U:delayed-coker.statement: The coker takes the heaviest oil in the plant and cooks it at high temperature in big drums until it breaks apart. It leaves behind a hard black solid called petroleum coke and gives off lighter oils that can be made into fuel.
U:delayed-coker.title: Delayed coker

U:desalination.statement: This plant makes fresh water from seawater by pushing it through very fine membranes under pressure. The membranes let water through but hold the salt back, a method called reverse osmosis.
U:desalination.title: Seawater desalination

U:dhdt.statement: This unit cleans diesel by heating it with hydrogen over a catalyst. The hydrogen turns the sulphur in the diesel into hydrogen sulphide gas, which is then removed.
U:dhdt.title: Diesel hydrotreater

U:flare.statement: The flare is the plant's safety valve. If a unit has a problem and gas must be released fast, the gas goes up a tall stack and burns in a controlled flame instead of escaping unburned.
U:flare.title: Flare system

U:grid-export-line.title: Grid line to the Kenyan grid, later (entry point at the fence)

U:hydrogen.statement: This plant makes pure hydrogen by reacting a light hydrocarbon feed (in this concept, hydrotreated light naphtha) with steam over a catalyst in a furnace, a step called steam methane reforming. A pressure swing unit then separates the hydrogen from the other gases.
U:hydrogen.title: Hydrogen plant (SMR + PSA)

U:isomerisation.statement: This unit reshapes the molecules of light naphtha from straight chains into branched chains, without changing the atoms. Branched molecules have a higher octane rating, so they make better petrol.
U:isomerisation.title: Isomerisation (for example Penex-DIH)

U:kht.statement: This unit cleans kerosene by treating it with hydrogen over a catalyst. The treatment removes sulphur and other impurities, and the product is meant to meet jet fuel specifications.
U:kht.title: Kerosene hydrotreater

U:marine.statement: The marine terminal is where ships load and unload. Single point moorings are floating buoys joined to the shore by pipe. In this concept two take in crude oil from large tankers offshore and three load petrol, diesel and jet fuel for export. Jetties at the port handle the smaller product ships.
U:marine.title: Marine (jetties, SPMs, subsea lines)

U:mild-hydrocracker.statement: This unit treats heavy gas oil with hydrogen and a catalyst under pressure. The hydrogen removes sulphur and breaks some of the large molecules into diesel, kerosene and naphtha.
U:mild-hydrocracker.title: Mild hydrocracker

U:nht.statement: This unit cleans naphtha, the light liquid that is the raw material for petrol. Hydrogen and a catalyst strip out sulphur and other impurities, and the clean naphtha is split into a light part and a heavy part.
U:nht.title: Naphtha hydrotreater (incl. coker naphtha section)

U:petcoke-cfb-power.statement: This power plant burns petroleum coke in circulating fluidised bed boilers, where hot air lifts the burning fuel so it moves like a liquid and limestone mixed in catches sulphur. The boilers make steam that drives turbines for electricity and also supplies steam to the process units.
U:petcoke-cfb-power.title: Petcoke CFB power, Phase 1 (2 boilers)

U:petcoke-cfb-power-phase-2.title: Petcoke CFB power, Phase 2 (about 2 boilers, about 500 MW for the Kenyan grid)

U:polypropylene.statement: This plant joins propylene gas molecules into long chains to make polypropylene, a common plastic. The plastic leaves as small pellets that customers melt and mould into products.
U:polypropylene.title: Polypropylene plant

U:propane-dehydrogenation.title: Propane dehydrogenation (propane to propylene; not confirmed)

U:rfcc.statement: This unit breaks heavy oil into lighter, more valuable molecules by mixing hot oil with a fine powder of catalyst, a material that speeds up a chemical change without being used up. The powder flows like a fluid, and the products are mainly petrol, propylene and light gases.
U:rfcc.title: Residue fluid catalytic cracker (with unsaturated gas plant and propylene recovery)

U:rgdu.statement: This unit removes sulphur from the petrol made in the cracker, using hydrogen and a catalyst. It is designed to lose as little octane as possible, and octane is the measure of how well a fuel resists knocking in an engine.
U:rgdu.title: RFCC gasoline desulphurisation

U:sat-gas-plant.statement: This unit collects the light gases that come off the distillation columns and sorts them into fuel gas, propane, butane and light naphtha. Saturated means the gas molecules have no reactive double bonds, so they are stable and easy to handle.
U:sat-gas-plant.title: Saturated gas plant

U:solids-handling.statement: This area moves the solid materials around the site. Coke is cut out of the coker drums with high-pressure water, crushed, stored and carried by conveyor belts, and limestone and ash are handled here too.
U:solids-handling.title: Solids handling (coke cutting, crushing, storage, conveyors; limestone; ash)

U:sour-water.statement: This unit cleans the dirty water that comes out of the process units, which has hydrogen sulphide and ammonia dissolved in it. Steam is blown through the water to drive those gases out.
U:sour-water.title: Sour water strippers

U:sulphur-recovery.statement: This unit turns hydrogen sulphide gas into liquid sulphur using the Claus process, in which part of the gas is burned and the rest reacts with the combustion products over a catalyst. A tail-gas section then catches what is left.
U:sulphur-recovery.title: Sulphur recovery (Claus + tail-gas treating)

U:tana-pipeline.title: Tana River water pipeline (entry point at the fence)

U:tank-farm.statement: The tank farm is the storage area, where big tanks hold the crude oil before it is processed and the finished products before they are shipped. Blending also happens here, where components are mixed to make finished petrol, diesel and jet fuel.
U:tank-farm.title: Tank farm (incl. blending)

U:utilities.statement: These are the shared services that all the units depend on: steam, cooling water, compressed air, nitrogen and fuel gas. Think of them as the plumbing, wiring and boiler room of the site.
U:utilities.title: Utilities (steam, seawater cooling, air, nitrogen, fuel gas)

U:vdu.statement: This unit boils the heavy residue from the first distillation again, this time under a strong vacuum so the oil boils at a lower temperature and does not burn. It splits the residue into vacuum gas oil, which can still become fuel, and a very heavy vacuum residue.
U:vdu.title: Vacuum distillation unit

U:water-treatment.statement: This area prepares water for use and cleans it afterwards. It makes demineralised water, which has had its dissolved minerals removed, for the steam boilers, and it treats the plant's waste water before it is discharged.
U:water-treatment.title: Water treatment (demin, boiler feed water, wastewater)
